A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hybrid Training (HyT) work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across relocated and redesigned material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ClevrSkills and LIBERO evaluations, inference-modality experiments, and real-world robot results, including Figures 3–5 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds coefficient and training-component ablations in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The act/think/follow distributions, Monte Carlo training objective, modality-controlled inference, and default weights (0.25, 0.5, 0.25) remain unchanged. The additional coefficient configurations are experimental ablations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine ClevrSkills tasks, four LIBERO suites, and real-world in-distribution and out-of-distribution manipulation tasks. The new difficulty groups reorganize existing tasks, and the new oracle ablation uses an existing test scenario.

E2.justification: ClevrSkills retains VLA, ECoT, and HiRobot as comparison methods; the LIBERO comparator rows in Figure 5 and the OpenVLA comparison in Table 1 are unchanged. The added coefficient variants serve as internal HyT ablations.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds controlled training-mixture configurations, including removing thought prediction or follow training. A.2 adds difficulty-group aggregation at 300 and 3000 demonstrations. Existing benchmark splits, evaluation budgets, model configurations, and default training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's data-scaling and oracle-modality studies, v2 adds coefficient sensitivity across data scales and a direct with/without-follow ablation for oracle instruction following (Figures 6–7). It also analyzes performance by task difficulty (A.2), substantially expanding evidence about component contributions and where HyT helps.

E5.justification: Standard-error reporting and evaluation of checkpoints at epochs 5, 7, and 10 are retained. The additional plots extend existing uncertainty displays without introducing new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 6–7 add substantial new outcomes on coefficient sensitivity and follow training, while A.2 adds difficulty-group summaries. Main results remain unchanged, including HyT's 93.7 LIBERO average and 63% real-world success. Matched hard/medium task endpoints reproduce v1 Figure 6, but intermediate per-task VLA/HiRobot scores are no longer displayed. Figure 10 duplicates the Place At (2 obj) results, compromising its claimed three-task easy-group summary.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1, Equations 1–3, distribution factorizations, and conditional-independence statements are unchanged. Removing redundant motivational prose does not alter the mathematical formulation; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal performance, inference-speed, and flexibility claims remain intact. Section 6 strengthens the outlook from complex tasks possibly benefiting from test-time thoughts to memory/advanced-reasoning tasks benefiting from them, and explicitly presents HyT as scalable distillation of human and foundation-model knowledge.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect thought prediction to stronger supervision with scarce data, follow training to better use of oracle instructions, and reasoning supervision to larger benefits on difficult tasks. Section 6 further discusses memory-dependent tasks and predicts declining annotation costs; these are interpretations and expectations, not newly tested capabilities.

D1.justification: Figures 6–7 disclose coefficient combinations for the new ablations. Existing hardware, optimization settings, prompts, thought-extraction pipelines, and access information are retained. One new legend lists t=0.2, a=0.8, f=0.2, totaling 1.2 despite the sampling-probability description, leaving that configuration ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds OneTwoVLA and π0.5 citations, links dynamic modality switching to OneTwoVLA, and expands the discussion of Chen et al. to include co-training and representation learning. These are limited positioning updates; neither newly cited method becomes an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: v2 removes duplicated method explanations, unfinished experimental prose, and redundant appendix references, and adds conference-header and affiliation text. The appendix separates coefficient analysis, difficulty analysis, and implementation details, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The appendix receives a substantial visual redesign: new coefficient and follow-ablation plots, plus three difficulty-group bar charts replacing the original four-method per-task learning-curve display. Existing examples and setup images are relocated and renumbered. Main figures and tables remain unchanged; Figure 10 introduces duplicated task panels.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations address v1's limited evidence for the chosen training mixture, and removal of duplicated draft prose improves clarity. These gains are tempered by Figure 6's inconsistent coefficient label and Figure 10's duplicated task results and misleading three-task summary. With the main method and benchmark results preserved, the revision provides a limited net improvement.
